escalations.summary: CrossPeak Solutions moved to Vensure (PEO) and completed benefits enrollment in December 2025, effective January 1, 2026. Vensure's 2026 Benefits Presentation described the coverage as the "2026 plan year," effective "January 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026." Beginning in March 2026 — roughly three months after enrollment — Vensure began telling CrossPeak that its ancillary benefits (dental, vision, life, disability, accident, and similar lines) actually run on a July 1–June 30 master plan year and would lapse on June 30, 2026 unless employees actively re-enrolled during a June 17–24 window. This July 1–June 30 ancillary cycle and the active re-enrollment requirement were never disclosed during sales or onboarding. Across roughly nine email threads over eight months, multiple Vensure representatives gave inconsistent answers or non-answers, and a documented commitment to review the contract for ancillary timelines went unanswered. The dispute over what CrossPeak was sold versus what Vensure now asserts remains open; CrossPeak has requested a call with Vensure leadership. On June 17, 2026, CrossPeak confirmed that the signed Benefit Election Contract does state coverage is effective through June 30, 2026 — a detail CrossPeak did not catch and that Vensure never pointed out; the core failure is that this was never surfaced during onboarding.

note.title: Update — Vensure granted the exception
note.html:
Update (June 18, 2026): after escalation, Vensure's benefit leadership approved an exception. Per AVP Brittany Shively, Vensure is "shutting down the ancillary open enrollment"; CrossPeak's ancillary benefits will now align with the January 1 renewal of the medical plan for all future renewals, and CrossPeak "will not be required to renew ancillaries on the 7/1 renewal date." This removes the June 30 lapse risk and the forced mid-year re-enrollment — the outcome CrossPeak asked for.

Confirmed June 17, 2026: the signed Vensure Benefit Election Contract (BEC) does state that the elections and rates are "effective through June 30, 2026." In fairness, that language is in the document CrossPeak signed, and Zane did not catch it at signing.

The issue CrossPeak is raising is not that the date is missing — it is that no one at Vensure ever mentioned, flagged, or walked through the June 30 ancillary cutoff during sales, signing, or onboarding, while Vensure's own 2026 Benefits Presentation simultaneously described the coverage as the "January 1 – December 31, 2026 plan year." Surfacing a buried, consequential end date is exactly what a PEO's onboarding is supposed to do.

impact: Vensure first told CrossPeak it had to move onto Vensure’s July 1 benefits cycle (‘All Vensure Master Plans renew on 7/1 annually’). That turned out not to be required: Vensure granted a January 1 alignment on 6/18, and by September was offering CrossPeak a 1/1/2027 medical go-live.
Roughly two weeks' notice on a hard deadline: ancillary coverage lapses June 30, 2026 if enrollment is not completed.
Risk that employees lose ancillary coverage through no fault of their own.
Vensure's own 2026 Benefits Presentation presented a January 1–December 31, 2026 plan year, contradicting the June 30 cutoff Vensure now asserts.
The July 1–June 30 ancillary cycle was never disclosed at sale or onboarding — it first surfaced in March 2026, about three months after enrollment.
Multiple Vensure representatives gave inconsistent or non-answers; a commitment to review the contract for ancillary timelines was never fulfilled.

escalations.summary: When CrossPeak migrated from Engage PEO to Vensure in late 2025, Vensure did not complete CrossPeak's state employment-tax registrations and access in four states — South Carolina, California, Georgia, and Illinois. It surfaced in March 2026, then stalled on a recurring blocker: CrossPeak's FEIN already had existing state accounts, so Vensure could not register new ones and instead needed either CrossPeak's portal logins or third-party-agent authority via signed POAs. Over the following months CrossPeak signed every POA requested and personally regained access to each state portal, while repeatedly asking Vensure to name one accountable owner and to hold a working call with its tax lead. By mid-May the items were in their 34th week; Zane requested a call three times between 5/27 and 6/8 with none scheduled, and Vensure's 5/14 status update omitted California entirely. A tax-team call occurred 6/10. On 6/16 Vensure's payroll-tax SVP clarified the South Carolina SUITS roles — the payroll-tax agent is Cohesive Networks 2 Inc (SC8P2J), while the conflicting agent Vensure TPA LLC (SC9Z6Y) handles unemployment claims only — giving CrossPeak the direction to reassign the wage and payment roles. Georgia's DOL-1N reactivation was acknowledged by the GDOL Office of Adjudication on 6/18 and is in its processing queue. As of late June the matter is in roughly its 40th week, and CrossPeak still has no written confirmation that the overdue state filings have been completed.
impact: Four states (SC, CA, GA, IL) without confirmed Vensure tax access for roughly 40 weeks after migration — risk of late or missed employer state tax filings for Q1–Q2 2026.
Potential penalty/interest exposure; CrossPeak has no written confirmation of filing status per state or of who covers penalties under the Client Service Agreement.

Georgia: the DOL-1N reactivation was submitted 6/10 and acknowledged by GDOL on 6/18 as in its processing queue (confirmation letter to be mailed) — access not yet restored.

note.html:
Update (July 15, 2026): resolved. Vensure found the root cause — the two hires were entered manually, and manual entry does not trigger onboarding. It relaunched onboarding for one hire, and CrossPeak collected the other hire’s signatures itself. Future hires now sign CrossPeak’s templates during e-onboarding.

As originally reported — as of June 26, 2026, Vensure has still not delivered CrossPeak's policy and agreement templates to its two new hires for signature. With Vensure stalled, CrossPeak has been forced to send these documents out for signature on its own — the exact onboarding function CrossPeak pays Vensure, as its PEO, to perform.

Vensure needs to get CrossPeak's templates into the onboarding workflow and out to its staff for signature now — measured in days, not a multi-week queue.

escalations.summary: When CrossPeak migrated from Engage to Vensure, Vensure's implementation scope covered only tax and payroll setup — it never requested CrossPeak's existing-employee hire paperwork or its new-hire policy, handbook, and agreement templates, and none were ever loaded into the onboarding workflow. Zane raised the question of company onboarding documents repeatedly from January onward, and the May 15 'responsibilities' outline assigned no owner for template creation. The gap surfaced concretely on Monday 6/15/2026 when two new hires — T.M. and O.S. — started and received nothing to sign. Only on 6/16 was CrossPeak first told in writing that the finished templates had to come from CrossPeak; CrossPeak rebuilt them overnight and delivered them. On 6/17 Vensure said the new templates will take its Client Solutions team '2+ weeks' to process, and separately ruled that NDAs, non-competes, confidentiality, arbitration, and employment-contract documents are not permitted in the onboarding workflow at all.
impact: Two new hires started 6/15/2026 with no CrossPeak policy, handbook, or agreement documents to sign — no executed acknowledgements for either.

escalations.summary: Two new hires (T.M. and O.S.) started June 15, 2026 under Vensure. On June 23 Vensure's system emailed CrossPeak to complete Section 2 of Form I-9 for T.M.; on June 25 CrossPeak's Service Operations Supervisor at Vensure said the pending I-9 approval was 'causing a halt to the Payroll.' When CrossPeak attempted to complete it, the PrismHR approval link did not work and no item appeared in CrossPeak's approvals queue — CrossPeak confirmed 'There is no I-9 awaiting approval.' Form I-9 Section 2 is the employer's responsibility and is normally due within three business days of the hire's first day (T.M. started 6/15, already past), yet the record Vensure pointed to was not actionable on CrossPeak's side — a catch-22 in which Vensure says payroll is halted while CrossPeak cannot clear the block as presented. Separately, O.S. was held off the payroll sheet pending banking and tax-withholding information. By June 26 both of CrossPeak's assigned Vensure contacts were out of office until June 29 with payroll still pending.

escalations.summary: While preparing the 2027 medical renewal on September 24, 2026, CrossPeak found that three employees who left earlier in the year — C.W. (termed 3/1/2026), A.K. (4/14/2026) and P.D. (5/4/2026) — were still enrolled and being billed on CrossPeak’s self-funded Trustmark medical plan. Vensure had terminated all three in payroll on time, but nothing carried those terminations to the broker or the carrier: the broker report access discussed at onboarding in December 2025 had not been set up, so no one outside Vensure could see hires or terminations. The same gap affected one July hire (H.R.), whose enrollment had not reached the carrier. Once it surfaced, every party engaged: Vensure gave the broker access on 9/29 and met with CrossPeak the same day; Trustmark approved an exception on 9/30 honoring the actual termination dates; and Vensure, UNIQ and CrossPeak are now confirming the hire and termination process end to end so it cannot repeat.

note.title: Where this stands — working together toward closure
note.html:
Recovered: Trustmark’s upper management approved an exception on 9/30 that ends coverage on the actual termination dates (C.W. 4/1, A.K. 5/1, P.D. 6/1). That should credit back nearly all of the ~$25.7K billed after the departures; $323.04 in claims paid in those months goes back to Trustmark. CrossPeak has asked Trustmark to confirm the credit in writing.

Fixed: the broker has had access to Vensure’s system since 9/29, and his first review found the one new hire whose enrollment had not reached the carrier. That enrollment has been submitted, and Vensure has set up the refund of the premiums deducted while it was pending.

Next: Vensure’s Head of Delivery, Nick Smith, is setting up two or three walkthroughs of the hire and termination process with CrossPeak and the broker, and Vensure and UNIQ will align on Trustmark’s new enrollment portal requirement before 11/1/2026.

impact: About $25.7K in medical premiums was billed for three former employees from April through September 2026.

Trustmark recovered about $4.8K on 9/28 and on 9/30 approved an exception honoring the actual termination dates (C.W. 4/1, A.K. 5/1, P.D. 6/1), which should cover nearly all of the rest; $323.04 in claims paid in those months is to be refunded to Trustmark.
One new hire (H.R.) had about $687 deducted from 8/14 while his enrollment had not reached Trustmark; the enrollment has been submitted and Vensure has set up the refund.
Until 9/29 no one outside Vensure could see hires or terminations; the broker’s new access closes that gap, and the walkthroughs will confirm the process end to end.
From 11/1/2026 Trustmark requires enrollment changes through its Manage My Group portal or an approved EDI feed.
